descriptor_toml:
[target]
type = "pmcp-run"
version = "1.0.0"

[aws]
region = "us-east-1"

[server]
name = "msr-vtt"
memory_mb = 512
timeout_seconds = 30

[environment]
RUST_LOG = "info"

[secrets]

[auth]
enabled = false
provider = "none"
callback_urls = []

[auth.dcr]
enabled = true
public_client_patterns = [
    "claude",
    "desktop",
    "cursor",
    "mcp-inspector",
    "chatgpt",
]
default_scopes = [
    "openid",
    "email",
    "mcp/read",
]
allowed_scopes = [
    "openid",
    "email",
    "profile",
    "mcp/read",
    "mcp/write",
]

[auth.scopes.custom]

[observability]
log_retention_days = 30
enable_xray = true
create_dashboard = true

[observability.alarms]
error_threshold = 10
latency_threshold_ms = 5000

[assets]
include = []
exclude = [
    "**/*.tmp",
    "**/.DS_Store",
    "**/Thumbs.db",
]

[composition]
tier = "foundation"
allow_composition = true
internal_only = false

# ============================================================================
# Operator-declared IAM
#
# `cargo pmcp deploy` regenerates `deploy/lib/stack.ts` from a built-in
# template on every deploy. Any hand-edits to `stack.ts` are wiped before
# `cdk synth`. The ONLY supported way to add Athena/Glue/S3 grants to the
# Lambda role is via these `[[iam.statements]]` blocks — they are spliced
# into the regenerated stack.ts as `addToRolePolicy(...)` calls.
#
# Resources use account=`*` because the renderer wraps each ARN in single
# quotes (no template-literal interpolation); the wildcard yields a
# portable ARN while the Lambda's own IAM can only authorise calls to its
# own account.
# ============================================================================

# Athena workgroup access (start/get/stop queries)
[[iam.statements]]
effect = "Allow"
actions = [
    "athena:StartQueryExecution",
    "athena:GetQueryExecution",
    "athena:GetQueryResults",
    "athena:StopQueryExecution",
    "athena:GetWorkGroup",
]
resources = [
    "arn:aws:athena:us-east-1:*:workgroup/msr-vtt",
]

# Glue catalog + database + table metadata for the msr_vtt database
[[iam.statements]]
effect = "Allow"
actions = [
    "glue:GetTable",
    "glue:GetTables",
    "glue:GetDatabase",
    "glue:GetDatabases",
    "glue:GetPartitions",
]
resources = [
    "arn:aws:glue:us-east-1:*:catalog",
    "arn:aws:glue:us-east-1:*:database/msr_vtt",
    "arn:aws:glue:us-east-1:*:table/msr_vtt/*",
]

# S3 access for MSR-VTT media + data buckets (read-only)
[[iam.statements]]
effect = "Allow"
actions = [
    "s3:GetObject",
    "s3:ListBucket",
    "s3:GetBucketLocation",
]
resources = [
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-media-*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-media-*/*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-data-*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-data-*/*",
]

# S3 access for Athena query results (read/write).
#
# Mirrors the open-images pattern: workgroup results are expected to land in the data/media
# buckets under a dedicated `athena-results/` prefix, not the AWS-default
# `aws-athena-query-results-*` bucket. Verify before deploying:
#   aws athena get-work-group --work-group msr-vtt --profile mam-dev --region us-east-1 \
#     --query 'WorkGroup.Configuration.ResultConfiguration.OutputLocation'
# If the OutputLocation is in a bucket NOT matched below, add the bucket's ARN here.
[[iam.statements]]
effect = "Allow"
actions = [
    "s3:GetObject",
    "s3:PutObject",
    "s3:ListBucket",
    "s3:GetBucketLocation",
    "s3:AbortMultipartUpload",
    "s3:ListMultipartUploadParts",
]
resources = [
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-data-*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-data-*/athena-results/*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-media-*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::msr-vtt-media-*/athena-results/*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::aws-athena-query-results-*",
    "arn:aws:s3:::aws-athena-query-results-*/*",
]

McpRoleArn.Description: MCP Server Lambda execution role ARN (stable export for downstream stacks)
